review_notes: I read the whole target file. It has no simp attributes of its own. I read the Submodule.reflectionOperator API in ForTauCeti/.../Projection/Blocks.lean, where `reflectionOperator_apply` is @[simp] and unfolds to `2 • P x - x`. I also read downstream uses of reflectionDefect in DoubleAngleSpectrum, ReflectedDefectDoubling and ReflectionRestriction. Both findings are about missing simp-interface lemmas (a pointwise unfolding lemma and an involution lemma). I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about what simp actually does. The suggestion for finding 2 is the less certain of the two: I could not confirm whether simp already closes the double-reflection goal through other simp lemmas about starProjection.

findings.problem: `reflectionDefect` is a bare def with no simp-friendly unfolding lemma. Each proof about it either does `simp only [reflectionDefect, comp_apply, sub_apply, ...]` (lines 42, 60) or uses `unfold reflectionDefect` followed by `ext`/`change`. Downstream files do the same: `unfold reflectionDefect` in DoubleAngleSpectrum, ReflectedDefectDoubling and ReflectionRestriction, plus an explicit `change ... - A x = ...` at line 130 here and `change` at DoubleAngleSpectrum 211. Without a pointwise rule, the simp normal form of `reflectionDefect V A x` is either an opaque application or a fully unfolded term, depending on the caller.
findings.proposed_change: Add a pointwise lemma, tagged @[simp] if the project wants `reflectionDefect V A x` to normalise to the pointwise form: `theorem reflectionDefect_apply (U) [U.HasOrthogonalProjection] (A) (x : E) : reflectionDefect U A x = U.reflectionOperator (A (U.reflectionOperator x)) - A x`. Proof: `rfl`, or `simp [reflectionDefect]`. Optionally also add `reflectionDefect_def` for the operator-level unfolding. Then `reflectionOperator_comp_reflectionDefect`, `reflectionDefect_eq_zero_of_reduces` and the `change` on line 130 can use `simp only [reflectionDefect_apply, ...]` or `rw [reflectionDefect_apply]` instead of unfolding the definition or restating the goal. Do not make the full unfolding simp, so that `reflectionDefect` stays folded in operator-level goals.
findings.benefit: Callers get one stable pointwise form. This replaces `unfold`, `change` and `simp only [reflectionDefect]` boilerplate across at least five proofs in this file and downstream. It also avoids the unwanted expansion that comes from unfolding the definition together with the @[simp] `reflectionOperator_apply`.

have hinvol (y : E) :
      U.reflectionOperator (U.reflectionOperator y) = y := by
findings.problem: The pointwise involution `J (J y) = y` has no canonical simp lemma. Only the operator-level `reflectionOperator_involutive` exists, and `reflectionOperator_apply` is @[simp] and rewrites `J y` to `2 • P y - y`. So plain `simp` on `J (J y)` expands it into a nested projection expression instead of returning `y`. The file therefore re-derives the pointwise fact inside two proofs: as `hinvol` here and as `hinvol` at lines 57–59 of `reflectionDefect_eq_zero_of_reduces`. Both are built by `congrArg` plus `simpa only [comp_apply, id_apply]`, and then used with `rw`.
findings.proposed_change: In Projection/Blocks.lean, next to `reflectionOperator_involutive`, add a pointwise lemma `reflectionOperator_reflectionOperator (U) [U.HasOrthogonalProjection] (y : E) : U.reflectionOperator (U.reflectionOperator y) = y`. Prove it from `U.reflection_reflection`, as `reflectionOperator_involutive` already does. Tag it @[simp] if the project wants it to fire first. Because `reflectionOperator_apply` is also @[simp], the project would need to check which rule simp applies to `J (J y)`. Simp rewrites inner subterms first, so the outer `J (J y)` pattern might not be tried. If that turns out to be a problem, give the new lemma higher priority or drop the @[simp] on `reflectionOperator_apply` in favour of explicit `simp [reflectionOperator_apply]`. Then replace both local `hinvol` blocks with the lemma.
findings.benefit: Removes the duplicated local proofs and gives downstream simp calls a canonical normal form for double reflections. Without the lemma, simp's only available rule for reflections is the expansion `2 • P x - x`.
